HISTORICAL_REVISION.NOTE: The former ISSUE32 plan was approved for its reviewed revision only. Its references to existing /v2 handlers, cutover-time route removal, and the prior transition approach are retained solely as provenance and are not normative for this clean-target proposal.

DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.EFFECTIVE_SPECIFICATION: This proposed DevelopmentPlan revision is derived from the exact Human-approved RequirementsAnalysis.xml revision ISSUE32-CLEAN-TARGET and Technology.xml revision ISSUE32-CLEAN-TARGET. It proposes one unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree, a separate /ws WebSocket endpoint, session-bound DPoP through existing Internal Auth UDS, current per-subscription membership authorization, immediate revocation enforcement, and a clean PostgreSQL 18.4 target-only schema. It does not authorize implementation, database changes, migration execution, merge, deployment, or changes to other repositories.

ISSUE48_DEVELOPMENT_REVISION.SCOPE: Define the target architecture, module boundaries, data responsibilities, request/event flows, consistency rules, dependencies, development order, invariants, and mental verification scenarios for the approved clean target. The proposal is architecture only. No source code, tests, SQL migrations, database schema files, runtime configuration, deployment, or other GRACE artifact is changed by this stage.

SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.SOURCE: Human-approved clean-target requirements are normative for behavior and acceptance.
Human-approved clean-target technology decisions are normative for technology choices and constraints.
SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.RULE: Existing code, historical DevelopmentPlan statements, historical approvals, and old migration files are not target-architecture authority when they conflict with the approved clean-target artifacts.

ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.PRINCIPLE: The only conversation HTTP resource tree is /conversations and its unversioned descendants. /ws is a separate WebSocket endpoint. No /v1 or /v2 HTTP routes, route aliases, compatibility facades, or legacy-client paths exist in the target.
Authentication proves a BFE Drive session using existing Internal Auth UDS and session-bound DPoP; conversation membership and role authorization remain independent application decisions.
Direct and group conversations use one conversation identity, one message-ordering model, one history model, one membership-visibility model, and one real-time delivery policy.

Membership changes, message ordering, history visibility, subscription authorization, and revocation must share a defined per-conversation ordering boundary. A connection or prior authorization result is not a permanent grant.

The target is bootstrapped from a clean target-only Goose migration chain on PostgreSQL 18.4. No legacy-data migration, obsolete schema/table/function/package, compatibility layer, or running-environment change is part of the target.
Chat stores only optional document ID and title metadata. It neither copies document content nor grants or proxies BFE Drive document rights.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Expose the sole unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree through Go net/http; apply request-size and shape limits; pass authenticated principal context to application use cases; map domain outcomes to stable HTTP responses.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not validate DPoP cryptography itself, decide membership/roles, implement persistence, publish Centrifuge events, expose /v1 or /v2, or preserve old route aliases.
MODULE.INTERFACE: Protected HTTP request -> DP48-M-AUTH -> DP48-M-APPLICATION; response returns through the same transport after the application outcome is known.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Call the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth UDS contract; validate session-bound DPoP proof and request binding for every protected HTTP request and each /ws connection; produce the trusted authenticated account UUID and authentication context.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not treat an account UUID alone as authorization, does not use Bearer fallback, does not decide conversation membership or group roles, and does not change the external Internal Auth contract.
MODULE.FAILURE_RULE: Missing, invalid, replayed, or misbound proof and Internal Auth failure fail closed before protected state changes or data disclosure.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-WS REQ32-AUTH REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-REALTIME TD32-SECURITY INV32-WS
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Keep /ws as the distinct WebSocket endpoint; authenticate connection establishment; independently authorize each requested conversation subscription using current membership interval and visibility state; associate each accepted subscription with the current membership interval/authorization generation; handle subscription invalidation and reconnect handoff.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: An authenticated connection alone grants no conversation access. The module does not trust a previous subscription decision after membership change and does not implement conversation business rules or persist messages.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-MODEL REQ32-DIRECT REQ32-GROUP REQ32-ROLES REQ32-MESSAGE REQ32-HISTORY REQ32-READ REQ32-DOCUMENT TD32-DOMAIN
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Coordinate use cases, domain validation, transaction boundaries, authorization checks, and typed success/failure outcomes across the domain modules. Ensure all use cases receive the principal produced by DP48-M-AUTH and use the same conversation authorization policy.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not own HTTP routing, DPoP verification, raw SQL, Centrifuge transport details, or BFE Drive document authorization.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Create and resolve direct conversations for two distinct authenticated account UUIDs; maintain one stable conversation identity per unordered account pair; apply caller-scoped personal hide without deleting or changing peer-visible conversation state or messages.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not authenticate the caller, implement group roles, erase messages, change peer visibility, or use legacy owner-scoped direct-chat structures.
MODULE.CONSISTENCY: Concurrent create attempts for the same normalized unordered pair converge on one direct conversation through a database-enforced uniqueness invariant and transaction-safe conflict handling. Self-direct requests are rejected without side effects.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-GROUP REQ32-ROLES REQ32-MODEL AC32-GROUP AC32-ROLES TD32-DOMAIN
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Create and manage named group conversations, membership changes, rename, departure, role assignment/removal, and ownership transfer. Enforce maximum 100 members including owner; exactly one owner remains after every successful mutation; owner transfers ownership before leaving and cannot leave if no other current member exists.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not infer Chat privileges from BFE Drive ADMIN, authenticate sessions, implement direct-pair uniqueness, or bypass membership visibility rules.

AUTHORIZATION_MATRIX.RULE: Owner may manage the group and appoint or dismiss admins while preserving exactly one owner.
Admin may perform only the expressly allowed member-management and rename operations; admin cannot remove the owner or another admin, appoint admins, or transfer ownership.
Member cannot perform group administration. A BFE Drive ADMIN role alone grants no Chat membership or group-management right.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-ROLES REQ32-HISTORY REQ32-WS REQ32-REALTIME INV32-WS INV32-PRESERVE
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Own the authoritative membership intervals, active membership lookup, group role checks, per-conversation authorization ordering, visibility boundaries, authorization-generation changes, and revocation decisions consumed by HTTP, history, WebSocket, and delivery paths.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not authenticate a BFE Drive session, own message content, or grant document access.
MODULE.VISIBILITY_RULE: Each membership interval has an inclusive visible_from_message_seq and exclusive visible_until_message_seq. History visibility is evaluated against each message sequence and the caller's own interval; messages in a gap between intervals remain invisible after rejoin. An active interval has no visible_until boundary.
MODULE.ORDERING_RULE: Membership mutation and message-sequence allocation serialize on the same conversation row inside PostgreSQL transactions. On join, visible_from_message_seq is set to the next message sequence to be allocated; on removal, visible_until_message_seq is set to the next sequence to be allocated. A send allocates and inserts its sequence under the same lock, so join/send and removal/send races have one database-defined order. Visibility remains visible_from_message_seq inclusive and visible_until_message_seq exclusive.
MODULE.REVOCATION_RULE: After removal/revocation commits, protected HTTP operations and new subscriptions fail immediately. The old membership interval/generation is invalidated, existing Centrifuge subscriptions for that interval are revoked, and delivery routing must not target that old interval. Delivery rechecks current authorization rather than relying on a cached connection or historical subscription decision.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-MESSAGE REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-LIMITS AC32-MESSAGE AC32-LIMITS TD32-DOMAIN
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Accept messages only from current members; derive sender identity from authenticated context; validate text and request limits; allocate one stable monotonic message sequence per conversation; enforce idempotent retries and persist the canonical message result.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not trust client-supplied sender identity, publish before persistence, determine history pagination, or grant document access.
MODULE.IDEMPOTENCY_RULE: For a repeated key and identical request content, return the original persisted result. For the same key with different content, return HTTP 409 Conflict. Concurrent retries must not create duplicate messages. The uniqueness scope and exact content-equivalence definition are unresolved in the approved upper artifacts and are recorded as open questions below; they must be settled before the message contract is authored.
MODULE.ORDERING_RULE: Message sequence allocation and insertion occur in one transaction under the conversation ordering boundary. A failed validation or authorization check has no persistence or publication side effect.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Serve cursor-paginated persisted messages with default page size 50 and maximum 100; apply membership-interval visibility to every page and to reconnect/catch-up queries; preserve the conversation's stable monotonic message order.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not bypass current authorization, reveal messages from membership gaps, or use a separate direct/group history model.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Maintain one monotonic read marker per account and conversation, shared across devices; calculate unread counts only from visible messages sent by other accounts; enforce that a caller can advance only their own marker.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not mutate another member's marker or count messages outside the caller's visibility intervals.

MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Validate and persist optional document ID and title as message context, returning both in authorized history and message events without copying document content.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not fetch document contents, create Drive grants, infer document access from conversation membership, or replace BFE Drive's independent document authorization.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-PRESERVE REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-MESSAGE REQ32-HISTORY REQ32-READ REQ32-DOCUMENT TD32-DOMAIN TD32-MIGRATION TECH32-POSTGRESQL TECH32-PG18-COMPAT TECH32-PGX
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Own PostgreSQL persistence through the existing pgx dependency and explicit transactions. Persist conversations, normalized direct-pair identity, group membership intervals and roles, ordered messages/idempotency records, read markers, and any transactional event-outbox records needed by the delivery design. Enforce uniqueness, foreign-key, check, and ordering constraints that protect the approved invariants.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not retain obsolete owner-scoped legacy tables, legacy SQL functions, legacy-only packages, old schema variants, or compatibility views. It does not run migrations or modify a database in this stage.
MODULE.TARGET_SCHEMA: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs reside within the bfe_chat schema. Only the active Issue #32 conversation model belongs in the final target schema. PostgreSQL major 18, baseline 18.4, is the approved bootstrap baseline. The existing five-migration compatibility run is evidence for that historical set only; it does not require all five files or their legacy definitions in the final clean target-only Goose chain.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-REALTIME REQ32-WS REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-MESSAGE TD32-SECURITY TD32-DOMAIN TECH32-CENTRIFUGE INV32-WS
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Use embedded Centrifuge for authenticated, authorized real-time delivery. Publish only persisted message events; route only to currently eligible membership intervals; process authorization-generation changes and revoke old subscriptions; use persisted history for reconnect recovery.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Centrifuge channel subscription alone is not a membership authority. The module does not publish uncommitted messages, treat a connection as permanent authorization, or deliver a document grant/content payload.
MODULE.DELIVERY_DESIGN: Persist a delivery/outbox record in the same transaction as the message. Dispatch committed records in per-conversation order, re-evaluate current membership intervals before fan-out, and target membership-interval-specific subscription channels rather than a broad channel that could continue delivering to a removed member. On removal, invalidate the old interval/generation and revoke its established subscriptions. A delivery decision made before a revocation must be ordered before the revocation barrier; no delivery decision after the barrier may target the revoked interval.
MODULE.RECOVERY: Real-time publication is not the source of truth. The committed message history and cursor are authoritative; reconnect and catch-up read persisted history through DP48-M-HISTORY with the same visibility filtering.

MODULE.refs: REQ32-PRESERVE INV32-NO-LEGACY TD32-MIGRATION TECH32-POSTGRESQL TECH32-PG18-COMPAT TECH32-GOOSE BP32-CUTOVER
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Specify a clean target-only Goose migration chain for fresh PostgreSQL 18.4 bootstrap, including only active target entities and constraints required by this proposal.
MODULE.NON_RESPONSIBILITY: Does not migrate legacy data, inspect production data, run SQL migrations, modify an existing database, deploy, or preserve obsolete migrations solely for compatibility with historical schemas.

LOGICAL_DATA_MODEL.DATA_OBJECT: One stable conversation identity with type DIRECT or GROUP. Direct and group operations share message order, authorization, history, membership interval, read-marker, and realtime semantics; type-specific rules are applied by the relevant domain module.
A normalized unordered pair of distinct account UUIDs uniquely identifies one direct conversation. The database constraint, not a check-then-insert alone, is the final concurrency guard.

A bounded membership interval records account, conversation, role, visible_from_message_seq inclusive, visible_until_message_seq exclusive or open, and a generation/identity for subscription revocation. Rejoin creates a new interval; it never widens an earlier interval over a gap.

A persisted message records conversation identity, monotonic conversation-scoped sequence, trusted sender account UUID, validated text, optional document ID/title, and idempotency result identity. A message event is eligible for publication only after its transaction commits.

A uniqueness-enforced idempotency record binds the request key to the canonical request/result so concurrent retries cannot create duplicates. The exact key scope and content-equivalence rule remain open until clarified by the Project Owner or an approved upper artifact.
A monotonic last-read message sequence per account and conversation; updates are account-scoped and immediately shared by all devices through the same persistent record.

A transactional delivery record for committed message and authorization-generation events. It supports ordered dispatch and revalidation; it is internal PostgreSQL state, not a new external service or dependency.
Optional document ID/title metadata only. No document bytes, copied content, bearer credential, or Drive authorization grant is stored in Chat.

FLOW.refs: REQ32-API REQ32-AUTH REQ32-ISOLATION TD32-HTTP TD32-SECURITY INV32-DPOP
FLOW.NAME: Protected HTTP request
FLOW.RESULT: Only unversioned /conversations routes are registered. The principal comes from successful Internal Auth plus DPoP validation. Membership/role authorization and transaction checks precede protected reads or writes; failures return without side effects or data leakage.

FLOW.refs: REQ32-WS REQ32-AUTH REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-REALTIME TD32-SECURITY INV32-WS
FLOW.NAME: WebSocket connection and subscription
FLOW.RESULT: Connection establishment requires valid session-bound DPoP. Every conversation subscription independently checks current membership and visibility. The accepted subscription is bound to the current interval/generation and is revoked when that interval is removed or invalidated.

FLOW.NAME: Direct conversation creation
FLOW.RESULT: Reject self-direct. Normalize the unordered pair, enforce uniqueness in PostgreSQL, and make concurrent requests resolve to the same stable conversation identity. Personal hide is caller-scoped and never deletes or hides peer data.

FLOW.refs: REQ32-GROUP REQ32-ROLES REQ32-MEMBERSHIP AC32-GROUP AC32-ROLES TD32-DOMAIN
FLOW.NAME: Group and role mutation
FLOW.RESULT: Authorize the actor's current role inside the mutation transaction. Enforce the 100-member maximum, exactly one owner, transfer-before-owner-leave, role restrictions, and interval changes atomically. Rejected operations leave membership and ownership unchanged.

FLOW.refs: REQ32-MESSAGE REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-REALTIME REQ32-LIMITS AC32-MESSAGE TD32-DOMAIN
FLOW.NAME: Send and publish message
FLOW.RESULT: Validate limits and current membership, allocate sequence, resolve idempotency, and persist message plus outbox record atomically. Commit before publication. Dispatcher rechecks recipients and visibility; no uncommitted or duplicate message is published.

FLOW.NAME: History and reconnect catch-up
FLOW.RESULT: Use one stable message order and cursor pagination. Every query filters messages by the caller's membership intervals; reconnect and catch-up use the same persisted history query and cannot expose messages from membership gaps.

FLOW.NAME: Document metadata in a message
FLOW.RESULT: Persist and return only document ID/title metadata. No document content is copied and no Chat operation grants or implies Drive access.

FLOW.NAME: Read marker and unread count
FLOW.RESULT: Advance only the caller's marker monotonically; calculate unread counts from other senders' messages visible in the caller's membership intervals; expose the same persisted state on all devices.

FLOW.NAME: Membership removal and revocation barrier
FLOW.RESULT: Serialize removal against message-sequence allocation and delivery authorization. Close the interval, invalidate its generation, and prevent new protected operations/subscriptions. Revoke established subscriptions and ensure subsequent fan-out targets only currently authorized intervals; stale channel subscriptions receive no later protected events.

FLOW.refs: REQ32-PRESERVE INV32-NO-LEGACY TD32-MIGRATION TECH32-POSTGRESQL TECH32-PG18-COMPAT AC32-CLEAN-TARGET
FLOW.NAME: Clean database bootstrap design
FLOW.RESULT: Define only the target conversation schema and required constraints for fresh PostgreSQL 18.4 bootstrap through Goose. The final migration chain does not carry obsolete schema, functions, packages, compatibility structures, or legacy-data migration steps. No migration is executed in this task.

INVARIANTS.INVARIANT: The target registers /conversations and its unversioned descendants as the sole conversation HTTP tree; /ws remains separate; /v1, /v2, and compatibility routes are absent.
Every protected HTTP request and /ws connection fails closed without a valid session-bound DPoP proof through Internal Auth UDS. Bearer-only credentials and account UUID alone are insufficient.

Each conversation subscription is authorized independently against current membership and visibility. A connection, cached result, or earlier subscription cannot grant continued access after revocation.
Messages are visible only within the viewer's own membership intervals. Rejoining creates a new interval and never exposes messages from the gap.
One unordered pair of distinct account UUIDs maps to at most one direct conversation, including concurrent creation attempts; self-direct is rejected.
Every successful group mutation leaves exactly one owner; owner departure requires transfer to another current member; role capabilities are enforced independently of BFE Drive ADMIN.

Concurrent retries for the same idempotency key cannot create duplicate messages; identical-content replay returns the original result and different-content replay returns 409. Exact key scope and content equivalence remain open design inputs.
No message is published before its persistence transaction commits. Delivery is derived from committed records and rechecks current authorized recipients.
Membership removal/revocation blocks later protected operations and delivery on established subscriptions. Fan-out never targets a revoked membership interval/generation after the revocation barrier.
Chat stores document ID/title only and grants no document rights; BFE Drive remains the independent authority for document access.
Read markers are monotonic per account and conversation, shared across devices, and cannot be advanced by another account; unread counts exclude own messages and invisible messages.

Group name is at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; group membership is at most 100 including owner; JSON request body is at most 65536 bytes; message text is at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page size defaults to 50 and cannot exceed 100. Invalid input is rejected before state changes or publication.

ACCEPTANCE_CHECKS.CHECK: Route inventory shows only unversioned /conversations HTTP resources and the separate /ws endpoint; /v1, /v2, aliases, and compatibility paths are absent.
Valid session-bound DPoP succeeds; missing, invalid, replayed, misbound, or Bearer-only proof fails closed before side effects or protected data disclosure.

CHECK.refs: REQ32-WS REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-REALTIME TD32-SECURITY INV32-WS AC32-WS

ACCEPTANCE_CHECKS.CHECK: Valid DPoP connection does not let a non-member subscribe; every subscription is independently authorized; removing membership blocks subsequent delivery on established subscriptions.

Self-direct is rejected; concurrent creation for the same unordered pair yields one stable conversation; personal hide affects only caller visibility and does not delete messages or alter peer access.
Group creation at 100 members including owner succeeds and 101 is rejected; owner transfer/leave rules and owner/admin/member permissions hold under concurrent mutation attempts.
Joining starts a new visibility interval; removal ends it; rejoining never exposes messages from the gap; send and membership mutation have a deterministic serialized order.

Identical idempotent replay returns the original result, different content returns 409, concurrent replay creates one message, text limit 16384 UTF-8 bytes is enforced, and invalid requests cause no side effects.
History defaults to 50, allows at most 100, uses stable cursor ordering, and filters every page and reconnect catch-up through the caller's membership intervals.
Message history/events preserve document ID and title but contain no copied document content or implied Drive grant.
Read marker cannot decrease, cannot be changed for another account, is shared across devices, and unread counts exclude own and invisible messages.
Only committed messages are published; delivery rechecks current eligible intervals; revoked intervals are never later fan-out targets; reconnect recovers through authorized history.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: The target transport registry is inspected.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: Every HTTP route is enumerated and the WebSocket endpoint is listed separately.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only /conversations and unversioned descendants are conversation HTTP routes; /ws remains separate; /v1, /v2 and compatibility aliases are absent.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C02 DP48-C03 REQ32-AUTH REQ32-WS INV32-DPOP INV32-WS
MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A valid user session and a WebSocket connection attempt.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: Requests use valid DPoP, missing proof, misbound/replayed proof, Bearer-only auth, and a valid connection attempts a non-member subscription.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only valid bound DPoP authenticates; the non-member subscription is denied even on an authenticated connection; all rejected paths produce no protected data disclosure.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: Two distinct account UUIDs concurrently request the same direct conversation.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: Both requests race at creation, and a separate request attempts a self-direct.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Both concurrent requests resolve to the same direct conversation identity; self-direct is rejected without creating state.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C05 REQ32-GROUP REQ32-ROLES AC32-GROUP AC32-ROLES DP48-I-OWNER
MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A group with an owner, admins, and ordinary members.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: Each role attempts allowed and forbidden mutations; the owner attempts to leave before and after transfer; membership count reaches 100 and then 101.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only permitted role operations succeed; owner cannot leave without a transfer to another current member and cannot leave as last current member; exactly one owner remains; 100 is accepted and 101 rejected.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C06 REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-HISTORY AC32-MEMBERSHIP AC32-HISTORY DP48-I-VISIBILITY
MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: An account joins a group, is removed, and later rejoins after messages were sent in each period and in the gap.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: It requests history and reconnect catch-up after rejoining.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only messages inside its own membership intervals are visible; gap messages remain hidden; membership removal and message sequence allocation have a deterministic order.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C07 REQ32-MESSAGE REQ32-LIMITS AC32-MESSAGE AC32-LIMITS DP48-I-IDEMPOTENCY
MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A current member submits a message and concurrently retries the same idempotency key.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: Retries contain identical content, different content, and boundary-sized or oversized text.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: One persisted message is created; identical retry returns the original result; different content returns 409; 16384 UTF-8 bytes is accepted and larger text is rejected before mutation. Key scope/content equivalence must be resolved before the downstream contract.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A member requests history with no page size, a page size of 100, and a page size above 100, then reconnects after missing events.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: History and catch-up are read through the same authorization-filtered query.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Default is 50; maximum is 100; over-limit input is rejected; order is stable; messages outside the viewer's membership intervals are not returned.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A member sends a message with optional document ID and title.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: The message is persisted, returned in history, and published as an event.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Both metadata fields are preserved; document content is not copied; the Chat service does not grant Drive access or treat membership as document authorization.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C11 REQ32-REALTIME REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-WS AC32-REALTIME AC32-WS DP48-I-REVOCATION
MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A message transaction, a delayed publisher, an established member subscription, and a concurrent membership removal.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: The message commits before or after the removal's serialized authorization boundary and the dispatcher evaluates delivery.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only committed messages are eligible; delivery is ordered against the revocation barrier; dispatcher rechecks current membership and never targets a revoked interval after the barrier; reconnect uses authorized persisted history.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: Two devices for one account, another account's messages, own messages, and messages outside a visibility interval.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: The account advances its read marker and requests unread counts from either device.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: The marker is monotonic and shared; another account cannot advance it; unread counts include only visible messages from other senders.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.GIVEN: A fresh PostgreSQL 18.4 database and the proposed target-only Goose migration chain.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.WHEN: The chain is later validated in an explicitly authorized downstream stage.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Only active clean-target schema is created; no obsolete legacy tables/functions/packages or compatibility structures are created; no legacy-data migration is present. This issue itself executes no migration.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.refs: DP48-C13 DP48-C14 REQ32-ISOLATION REQ32-LIMITS AC32-ISOLATION AC32-LIMITS DP48-I-LIMITS
